    StartersMarigold bridge cornCharred corn with lime mayo, feta, chilli powder and corianderHow to make it4 corn cobs4 tbsp mayonnaise2 limes100g feta, crumbled1 tsp chilli powder2 tbsp chopped coriander1 tbsp orange nasturtium petalsGrill the corn until charred.Brush with mayonnaise mixed with lime juice.Roll in the feta, dust with chilli powder and coriander and scatter a few petals on top.Abuelita's tamalesPork and red chile tamales in masa doughHow to make it500g pork shoulder4 tbsp red chilli sauce300g masa harina100g lard1 tsp baking powder400ml warm chicken stock16 corn husks, soaked200g salsaSimmer the pork until tender, then shred and mix with the red chilli sauce.Soak the corn husks in warm water.Beat the masa with the lard, baking powder and stock to a soft dough.Spread on the husks, add the pork and fold.Steam for 60 minutes.Serve with salsa.Santa Cecilia plaza guacamole and totoposThe mariachi plaza in Santa CeciliaHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chunky guacamole with lime, chilli, onion and coriander, topped with pomegranate and toasted pepitas, with crisp fried corn tortilla chips.Cut 8 corn tortillas into wedges and fry at 180°C for 2 minutes until crisp, then salt.Mash 3 ripe avocados roughly with the juice of 2 limes and salt.Fold in half a finely diced white onion, 1 seeded chopped jalapeño, 1 diced tomato and a handful of coriander.Top with 2 tbsp pomegranate seeds and 2 tbsp toasted pepitas and serve with the warm chips.MainsRivera family enchiladasChicken enchiladas in a dried chile sauce, topped with cheeseHow to make it4 dried chillies1 garlic clove300ml chicken stock600g chicken thighs8 corn tortillas200g Monterey Jack, grated150g sour cream1 white onion, dicedSoak the chillies, blitz with the garlic and stock and simmer into a sauce.Poach and shred the chicken.Dip the tortillas in sauce, roll with chicken and some of the Monterey Jack, then cover with sauce and the rest of the cheese.Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes. Serve with sour cream and onion.Ofrenda red pork pozoleThe family's Day of the Dead tableHow to make itAs written, serves 4Pork shoulder and hominy simmered in a deep red chilli broth, topped at the table with shredded cabbage, radish, lime, oregano and crisp tostadas.Simmer 1.2kg diced pork shoulder in 2.5 litres water with 1 halved onion, 4 garlic cloves and 2 tsp salt for 1.5 hours.Soak 4 dried guajillo and 2 ancho chillies in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend with 2 garlic cloves and a little soaking water and strain into the pot.Add 2 drained tins hominy and simmer 30 minutes more.Serve with shredded cabbage, sliced radish, lime wedges, dried oregano and tostadas.SweetsPan de muertoSweet orange yeast bread topped with dough bonesHow to make it450g plain flour7g dried yeast180g caster sugar2 oranges, zested3 eggs120g butter, 80g soft and 40g melted100ml warm waterMix the flour, yeast, part of the sugar, orange zest, eggs, soft butter and warm water into a soft dough and knead.Prove for 2 hours.Shape into rounds with dough bones on top.Prove again for 30 minutes.Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.Brush with melted butter and roll in the remaining sugar.DrinksChampurradoThick Mexican hot chocolate made with masa, cinnamon and brown sugarHow to make it50g masa harina250ml water1 L milk100g dark chocolate1 cinnamon stick60g brown sugarWhisk the masa into the water until smooth.Heat the milk with the chocolate, cinnamon and sugar, then whisk in the masa.Simmer, stirring, until thick and silky. Pour into mugs.
